claims.statement: STEP 1: semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly led to 12.4 percentage points more body-weight loss than placebo at 68 weeks (adults with obesity, no diabetes).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Funded by Novo Nordisk (abstract); preregistered NCT03548935, NEJM. Funder-role section not accessible (paywall/403); funding taken from abstract statement. Scored at industry-pivotal midpoint. Quality: Large double-blind placebo RCT, 68 weeks, treatment-policy estimand handles discontinuation; weight is objective. Placebo comparator only.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24.

claims.statement: STEP 5: semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly led to 12.6 percentage points more body-weight loss than placebo at 104 weeks (adults with obesity, no diabetes).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Full text (PMC9556320) states funder designed the trial, collected and analyzed data, and paid medical writing; employee co-authors. Preregistered NCT03693430. Quality: Double-blind 2-year RCT with good retention, but small (n=304) for safety estimates.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24.

claims.statement: OASIS 4: oral semaglutide 25 mg daily led to 11.4 percentage points more body-weight loss than placebo at 64 weeks (adults with overweight or obesity, no diabetes).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Novo Nordisk-funded registered trial (NCT05564117), NEJM. Publisher page returned 403; funder-role and full COI sections not read. Sponsor stated in abstract. Quality: Double-blind 64-week RCT of the marketed dose; small (n=307) and attrition not reported in abstract.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24.

claims.statement: SURMOUNT-1: tirzepatide 15 mg weekly led to about 17.8 percentage points more body-weight loss than placebo at 72 weeks (-20.9% vs -3.1%; adults with obesity, no diabetes).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Lilly-funded pivotal trial in NEJM, preregistered (NCT04184622). Full-text funding/role-of-funder section not reachable (paywalled/403); funder role inferred from abstract funding line and Lilly employee co-authors [inference]. Quality: Large (n=2539) 72-wk double-blind placebo RCT with treatment-regimen ITT estimand; attrition details not in abstract.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24.

claims.statement: SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes: liraglutide 3.0 mg daily led to about 5.3 percentage points more body-weight loss than placebo at 56 weeks (5.6 kg difference; adults with obesity, no diabetes).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Abstract states 'Funded by Novo Nordisk'; preregistered (NCT01272219), NEJM. Full-text trial-oversight / funder-role section not accessible (NEJM returned 403); funder taken from abstract funding line only. Quality: Large (n=3731) 56-wk double-blind placebo RCT; primary analysis used LOCF imputation, which is weaker handling of missing data in an obesity trial with meaningful dropout.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24.

claims.statement: ATTAIN-1: orforglipron at the top trial dose (36 mg capsule) led to about 9.1 percentage points more body-weight loss than placebo at 72 weeks (-11.2% vs -2.1%; adults with obesity, no diabetes).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Abstract: 'Funded by Eli Lilly'; preregistered (NCT05869903). Full-text trial-oversight / funder-role section not accessible (NEJM returned 403); funder taken from abstract funding line only. Quality: Large double-blind placebo RCT, 72 wk, treatment-regimen estimand; attrition not given in abstract.

claims.statement: SELECT: in adults with heart disease and overweight or obesity but no diabetes, semaglutide 2.4 mg cut major heart events (heart attack, stroke, heart death) by 20% vs placebo (hazard ratio 0.80) over a mean follow-up of 39.8 months.

ratings.rationale: Bias: Novo Nordisk funded (abstract); preregistered NCT03574597, NEJM. Academic steering-committee and independent-analysis details not verified (NEJM 403). Would move to ~0.5 if confirmed. Quality: Very large event-driven double-blind CVOT with hard clinical endpoint and >3 y follow-up. Duration_weeks = 39.8 mo mean follow-up converted (~173 wk).

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24, including severity weights and scales.

claims.statement: SUSTAIN-6: in people with type 2 diabetes at high heart risk, injectable semaglutide (0.5 or 1 mg) cut major heart events by 26% vs placebo (hazard ratio 0.74).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Novo Nordisk funded (abstract); preregistered NCT01720446, NEJM. Funder-role section not accessible (paywall/403); funding taken from abstract statement. Quality: Double-blind CVOT with hard endpoints, but designed for noninferiority; superiority was not prespecified and event count modest (254 MACE). Retinopathy signal is a key safety finding.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24, including severity weights and scales.

claims.statement: SOUL: in people with type 2 diabetes and heart or kidney disease, oral semaglutide 14 mg cut major heart events by 14% vs placebo (hazard ratio 0.86).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Novo-funded, preregistered (NCT03914326), academic steering committee, NEJM. Sponsor role inferred from companion SOUL paper since NEJM page was blocked. Quality: Very large double-blind superiority CVOT with ~4 years follow-up and a hard clinical endpoint; modest absolute effect (1.8 pp).

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24, including severity weights and scales.

claims.statement: PIONEER 6: in people with type 2 diabetes at high heart risk, oral semaglutide had 21% fewer major heart events than placebo (hazard ratio 0.79), a result that could be due to chance (95% CI 0.57 to 1.11).

ratings.rationale: Bias: Novo Nordisk-funded, registered, NEJM-published CVOT. Publisher page returned 403; funder-role and full COI sections not read. Sponsor stated in abstract. Quality: Large double-blind event-driven trial but designed only for safety noninferiority; median 15.9 months, few events, so mortality findings are secondary and imprecise.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24, including severity weights and scales.

claims.statement: LEADER: in people with type 2 diabetes at high heart risk, liraglutide cut major heart events by 13% vs placebo (hazard ratio 0.87) over a median 3.8 years.

ratings.rationale: Bias: Oversight section read in PMC: academic-majority steering committee, independent DSMB, analysis by external CRO plus sponsor, first draft by academic authors; but sponsor employees co-author and sponsor-funded writing. Preregistered (NCT01179048). Quality: Large double-blind event-driven CVOT, median 3.8 y follow-up, hard clinical endpoint.

review.notes: Approved in Claude session 2026-11-24, including severity weights and scales.

gaps.detail: Its heart trial, SURPASS-CVOT, compared it with dulaglutide (another GLP-1 drug) rather than placebo, so it isn't scored here.
Its heart trial, ACHIEVE-4, compared it with insulin glargine and was designed to check heart safety, so it isn't scored here.

notices.text: Being discontinued: FDA lists brand Saxenda and the only generic weight-loss version (Teva's 3 mg pen) as "To Be Discontinued." Other generic liraglutide pens are for diabetes and go up to 1.8 mg. Check with your pharmacy before choosing this option.
